parameters.name: DeviceName
parameters.description:
The device name of the device for which you want to set desired property values.
><notice> If you specify this parameter, you must also specify **ProductKey**.
></notice>

parameters.name: IotId
parameters.description:
The ID of the device for which you want to set desired property values. This is the unique identifier issued by IoT Platform for the device.
><notice> **IotId** is the globally unique identifier of a device and corresponds to a combination of **ProductKey** and **DeviceName**. If you specify this parameter, you do not need to specify **ProductKey** or **DeviceName**. If you specify **IotId** together with **ProductKey** and **DeviceName**, **IotId** takes precedence.
></notice>

parameters.name: IotInstanceId
parameters.description:
The instance ID. On the **Overview** page in the IoT Platform console, you can view the **ID** of the current instance.

><notice>
- If this **ID** value exists, you must specify it. Otherwise, the call fails.
- If the **Overview** page or **ID** value is not available, you do not need to specify this parameter.

></notice>

For more information about instances, see [Overview](~~356505~~).

parameters.name: Items
parameters.description:
The desired property values to set, in **Key:Value** format. The data format is JSON String. Example: **{"Temperature":35}**. You can specify up to 10 desired property values.

- **Key** is the identifier of the property (**identifier**). You can view it in the **Feature Definition** of the product to which the device belongs in the console, or call [QueryThingModel](~~150321~~) to obtain it from the returned Thing Specification Language model data.

    If the property is temperature under a custom (non-default) module testFb, the parameter value is **{"testFb:temperature":35}**.

    > The specified property must be read/write. If you specify a read-only property, the setting fails. In a single call, you cannot pass duplicate property identifiers.
  


- **Value** is the desired property value to set. The value must conform to the data type and value range that you defined for the property.

    > If the property value is set to null, the desired property value is cleared.

parameters.name: ProductKey
parameters.description:
The ProductKey of the product to which the device belongs. The device is the one for which you want to set desired property values.
><notice> If you specify this parameter, you must also specify **DeviceName**.
></notice>

parameters.name: Versions
parameters.description:
The current version of the desired property values, in Key:Value format. The data format is JSON String. Example: {"Temperature":2}.

- **Key** is the identifier of the property (identifier). You can view the identifier of a property in the feature definition of the product to which the device belongs in the console.

    > In a single invoke, the key values (property identifiers) cannot be duplicated.

- **Value** is the current version number of the desired property value.

    When you set a desired property value for the first time, set this parameter to 0. After the first setting, the version number becomes 1. Each subsequent setting automatically increments the version number by 1 (for example, set this parameter to 1 for the second setting, and the version number automatically becomes 2 after success. Set this parameter to 2 for the third setting, and the version number automatically becomes 3 after success, and so on).
    > If the specified version number does not match the current version, the server will reject the request. If you are unsure of the current version number, you can omit the version number but must still pass valid JSON, that is, pass {}.
